text:
Nikita Kucherov asked the Lightning for a trade at the end of October, telling them, as the Associated Press reported, that he won't re-sign. A month later he is still in Tampa and still producing: a four-game point streak, and the 80% chance of a point our numbers give him tonight is the highest on either side. The headlines this week have moved to where he might go, with Montreal named most often, but every game he plays in a Lightning sweater is another one the standings remember. Tampa also lost Conor Geekie for four to five months after shoulder surgery.

Ottawa comes in with the better record and the hotter goalie. The Senators lead the Atlantic, three points ahead of Tampa, and Linus Ullmark has turned a rough 2025-26 (13.3 goals worse than his shots deserved) into a .935 season, 12.5 goals saved above expected, which measures goals allowed against the quality of shots faced. His win streak ended in Florida on Wednesday, a 5-3 loss, but he is .929 over his last five starts. Andrei Vasilevskiy, 23.2 above expected last season, is a more modest 2.5 this year.

There is very little between these teams in the run of play. Ottawa has taken 55% of the expected goals at five on five (the share of quality chances), Tampa 56%, and our numbers have it close: 3.05 expected goals for the Lightning, 2.86 for the Senators. Tampa's one clear edge is discipline. Ottawa takes 4.6 penalties a game, and the Lightning draw four.

Tim Stützle is the Senator to watch, who left Monday's game after a hard collision with a goalpost but is in our projected lineup, filling William Eklund's spot beside Dylan Cozens, who has six goals in his last 13 games. For Tampa, Brandon Hagel is back from injured reserve and our likeliest scorer at 40%, Victor Hedman is day-to-day and in our numbers, and this is the last game of a six-game home stand.
headline: Kucherov keeps producing while Tampa waits on his future
